skill.name: okx-defi
skill.description: Discover OKX-aggregated DeFi yields, inspect multichain positions, analyze liquidity, and prepare deposits, withdrawals, and reward claims through the onchainos CLI.
skill.summary: Compare DeFi products and manage position workflows with separate transaction preparation and wallet signing.
skill.author: okx

security_audit.summary: All 84 static matches are benign Markdown, DeFi parameters, documentation links, or explicit private-key noncustody language. Two semantic risks remain: automatic unpinned installer execution and signing opaque transaction responses without documented semantic verification. User confirmation and sequential execution mitigate some risk; no evidence found of credential exfiltration or audit-targeted prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Mandatory preflight runs an automatically approved, unpinned registry installer.
remediation.suggestion: Require installation consent, pin a reviewed installer version, verify package provenance, and skip installation when an acceptable CLI is already present.

remediation.issue: Opaque transaction fields are passed to signing without documented checks of their financial effects.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve payload bytes, but decode or simulate separately; verify chain, sender, target, approval spender, limits, and amounts before requesting explicit signing consent.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Unpinned Installer Execution
semantic_findings.description: The mandatory preflight delegates to a bundled fallback that runs npx -y @okxweb3/onchainos-installer without a package version pin. This permits mutable registry code to execute before ordinary queries, without a separate installation-consent step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The entry point requires preflight each thread, and the reviewed fallback specifies the unpinned npx command. No evidence found of malicious package contents.

semantic_findings.title: Opaque Transaction Signing Without Documented Semantic Verification
semantic_findings.description: The wallet flow passes returned targets, payloads, and values directly into signing and forbids inspecting rejected payloads. User confirmation is required, but no documented decoding or simulation verifies approval scope or intended asset movements before signing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Direct wallet signing and the inspection prohibition are explicit. External wallet safeguards may reduce exposure, but their implementation is outside these files.

content.user_title: Explore DeFi Yields and Manage Positions
content.value_statement: Comparing DeFi yields and tracking positions across chains requires consistent product, token, and wallet data. This skill guides OKX-aggregated discovery, portfolio inspection, and transaction preparation through the onchainos CLI.
actual_capabilities: Search OKX-aggregated earn, liquidity-pool, and lending products by token, chain, and product group.
Retrieve product APY, TVL, accepted tokens, and historical yield or TVL data.
Inspect multichain holdings, protocol positions, pending rewards, and lending health indicators.
Analyze V3 liquidity depth, relative-price history, NFT position identifiers, and tick ranges.
Prepare unsigned deposit, withdrawal, and reward-claim transactions with token precision and balance checks.
Guide sequential signing and broadcasting through a separate wallet workflow, with user confirmation and failure reporting.
limitations: Requires the external onchainos CLI and available OKX services; bundled preflight runs a registry installer.
Covers OKX-aggregated products only; dedicated companion skills handle named DApp discovery, token markets, and wallet operations.
Transaction preparation does not broadcast; signing requires an external wallet or the Agentic Wallet workflow.
Does not guarantee yield, contract safety, or successful execution; some reference examples conflict with documented precision and address rules.

prompt_templates.title: Find Yield Products
prompt_templates.prompt: Find supported USDC yield products on Ethereum. Show product identifiers, APY, and TVL. Do not prepare or sign transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Positions
prompt_templates.prompt: Show DeFi positions for [EVM address] on Ethereum and Base. Include protocol identifiers, pending rewards, and any available lending health warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Product History
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [investment ID A] and [investment ID B] using monthly APY and TVL history. Identify missing data and report observations without guaranteeing returns.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a V3 Withdrawal
prompt_templates.prompt: For [address], inspect V3 position [token ID] on [chain]. Refresh position details and prepare a full withdrawal only after confirming parameters. Do not sign.

best_practices: Confirm the wallet address, chain, product identifier, token precision, and amount before preparing transactions.
Refresh position details before each withdrawal or claim, and check available balances before deposits.
Review installer provenance and transaction effects before consent; execute approved steps sequentially and stop on failure.
anti_patterns: Selecting products only by advertised APY while ignoring liquidity, contract risk, or lending health.
Reusing stale positions, expired calldata, or amounts copied without checking token precision.
Signing opaque payloads without verifying recipients, approval limits, chain, and expected asset movements.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The environment also needs the external onchainos CLI.

faq.question: Does it cover every DeFi protocol?
faq.answer: No. Coverage depends on OKX aggregation and current supported chains and platforms. Named third-party DApp research routes to a companion skill.

faq.question: Can I inspect positions without logging into a wallet?
faq.answer: You can provide a public wallet address for position queries. The address must match the selected chain family.

faq.question: Does preparing a transaction move funds?
faq.answer: No. DeFi preparation returns unsigned calldata. A separate signing and broadcast workflow can move funds after user confirmation.

faq.question: What should I review before signing?
faq.answer: Verify the chain, signing address, contract target, approval spender, amounts, and expected asset movements. Use decoding or simulation without changing payload bytes.

faq.question: Are the displayed yields guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. APY and TVL can change, and DeFi positions carry financial and contract risks. The skill requires warnings for APY above 50%.
